findings.title: OS Command Injection
findings.trigger: An attacker could potentially inject malicious data into the input file that causes the program to behave unexpectedly.
findings.assumptions: The input file is controlled by an attacker and the data read from it is not properly sanitized before being processed.

findings.title: Buffer Overflow
findings.trigger: An attacker could provide a very large value for chunkSize, causing malloc to allocate an excessive amount of memory.
findings.assumptions: The chunkSize variable is controlled by an attacker and not properly validated.

findings.title: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
findings.trigger: An attacker could inject malicious data into the input file that could be sorted in a way to exploit the sorting function.
findings.assumptions: The data in the input file is controlled by an attacker and not properly sanitized before being sorted.

findings.title: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
findings.trigger: An attacker could inject malicious data into the input file that could be written to the output file in a way to exploit the write operation.
findings.assumptions: The data in the input file is controlled by an attacker and not properly sanitized before being written to the output file.
